messages:
hana.r: Quick heads-up - found a subtle SDK parity issue when combining Retrofit suspend calls, OkHttp callTimeout, and a custom upload helper. Duplicates in production logs after timeouts. Repro below.

hana.r: Repro env: Pixel 3a emulator (API 30), OkHttp 4.10, Retrofit 2.9, Kotlin coroutines. Our app wraps a streaming upload in withTimeout(7_000) but OkHttp client has callTimeout(10_000). Sometimes we see client cancel locally then server returns 200 and a later retry sends same payload again.

marc.d: Classic ambiguous outcome. If coroutine cancels before the socket fully reads server response, higher-layer retry may assume failure. Do you have any outer retry policy?

hana.r: Yes - we have an app-level retry that retries network failures once. It retries on TimeoutCancellationException, which is too coarse.

tomas.k: Two quick fixes: (1) prefer OkHttp's callTimeout as the canonical total timeout and avoid withTimeout around the network call, (2) if you must cancel at coroutine layer, inspect Call.isExecuted/response before retrying.

hana.r: Example of the bug: we call api.upload(body) inside withTimeout, coroutine throws, we catch and retry. But sometimes server already processed the first request and responded 200 just as we timed out. We didn't see response and retried -> duplicate.

marc.d: Also check HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1.1. H2 multiplexing can make stream errors a bit opaque; client cancel does not necessarily abort server processing.

hana.r: Tried disabling retryOnConnectionFailure and duplicates dropped in our smoke runs, but we worry about losing helpful automatic retries for idempotent endpoints.

tomas.k: SDK guidance idea: sample client builder should show two presets: "general" (default retryOnConnectionFailure=true) and "uploads" (retryOnConnectionFailure=false, shorter keepAlive). And docs should explicitly say: "If you use coroutine cancellations, do not blindly retry non-idempotent calls."

marc.d: Also add a helper in samples: a small wrapper that retries only if Call.finishedWithoutResponse()? Better: helper that translates network outcome into three states: success, definite-failure, ambiguous. Only retry on definite-failure.

hana.r: Here's a tiny helper idea (pseudocode):
```
val outcome = executeCallSafely(call)
when (outcome) {
  Success -> return
  Ambiguous -> surface error to app: "upload may have completed; please check server status before retry"
  DefiniteFailure -> retry
}
```

marc.d: Love it. Also include an example server-side idempotency header (X-Upload-Token) in samples so apps can avoid costly checks.

ci-bot: created ticket #5782: "android-sdk: document cancellations vs callTimeouts; add upload client preset" assigned to @tomas.k

hana.r: I'll open a PR with: (A) short doc section explaining ambiguous outcomes + checklist, (B) two sample client presets, (C) small executeCallSafely helper and a buffered RequestBody example (<4MB warning). Will run emulator matrix after.

tomas.k: Thanks. Also run with and without HTTP/2 to compare. Emulator network stack differences matter.

hana.r: Will do and paste results. Thanks for the quick help :slightly_smiling_face:
